title: The exact ten-point Heilbronn number in the unit square
statement: For P=(p_1,...,p_10) in ([0,1]^2)^10, let a(P)=min_(i<j<k) |det(p_j-p_i,p_k-p_i)|/2 and H_10=max_P a(P). Determine H_10 by an exact or rigorously certified attaining configuration and a matching upper bound over the full square configuration space.
source_locator: Monji et al. v1, Table 5 and Section 5; Sudermann-Merx v1, Section 7 and Appendix A, Table 11; v2, Sections 4.1, 5.6 and 7, and Appendix A, Table 11.
status_basis: Both inspected preprints leave unrestricted n=10 optimality unresolved; the 2026 paper supplies an exact incumbent. A scoped search through 2026-10-14 found no authoritative matching global bound. Inspection of Sudermann-Merx v2 on 2026-10-17 confirmed that n=10 certification remains a stated open direction and clarified the numerical precision of the reported optimization certificates. Solver-tolerance discrepancies in the 2025 paper are retained as unresolved numerical evidence.

revision_history.change: Added Sudermann-Merx v2 and corrected the distinction between an exact nine-point construction and a numerical global optimality certificate. The algebraic nine-point value is not adopted as a certified upper bound for H_10. The ten-point target and open-status category are unchanged.

epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No physical model, empirical data or experiment is needed.

novelty.basis: A future certified improvement must be compared with updated exact records; an alternative representation of the existing configuration is not a new bound.

plain_summary: Arrange ten points in a unit square so that the smallest of their 120 triangles is as large as possible. A better arrangement has a short exact certificate; proving that no better arrangement exists is much harder.
assumptions: Points lie in the closed Euclidean unit square, with no lattice, symmetry or prescribed boundary positions.
Every triple contributes its unsigned area, including zero for collinear or coincident points.
Numerical optimization is only a search method; certified lower bounds require exact arithmetic or rigorous intervals.
scope: Unrestricted ten-point optimization. The proposed first milestone seeks a certified improvement over a published exact configuration; it does not assume the current configuration is optimal.
target: Determine H_10. Curator-proposed first milestone: search the full twenty-coordinate space for a configuration whose rigorously verified minimum area exceeds L=(5/8)z^2-(1/2)z^3, where z=3/4-(63+8*sqrt(62))^(1/3)/12-1/(12*(63+8*sqrt(62))^(1/3)) and positive real roots are used.
success_criteria: A lower-bound improvement supplies ten exact rational or algebraic points in the square and a proof that all 120 triangle areas exceed L.
Cap the proposed exploratory search at 100 starting configurations, 4 CPU-hours and 8 GiB RAM; stop at the first cap reached. These limits define a manageable experiment, not a predicted requirement.
Refine promising floating-point outputs to exact coordinates or rigorous intervals. A solver-reported objective by itself is not a certified bound.

An exact solution also requires a matching upper bound for all configurations, with every reduction justified. A restricted-family optimum or local optimality certificate must retain that restricted label.
known_results: Appendix A, Table 11 of the 2026 preprint reproduces Comellas-Yebra coordinates and the exact lower bound L above; global optimality is explicitly unproved.

Sudermann-Merx gives an exact nine-point configuration with minimum triangle area -11/64+9*sqrt(65)/320 and reports numerical global optimization. Version 2, Section 4.1, qualifies the optimization certificate by solver precision. Although H_10 <= H_9, the algebraic value is not adopted here as a rigorously certified upper bound for H_10: exact coordinate recovery does not by itself prove global optimality. Any upper bound used in a future argument needs its own checked justification.

The 2025 paper's n=10 model uses unproved restrictions. Its Table 5 distinguishes solver objective 0.0465383 from recomputed minimum area 0.0465369; this card does not adopt the larger floating-point value as an exact bound.
prerequisites: Interval certification and the difference between local and global optima
significance: A certified improved arrangement would strengthen a classical finite geometric bound. A rigorous global upper bound would settle an unresolved exact case; negative local searches alone do neither.

requirements.data: The exact reference points are in SRC-MATH-205, Appendix A, Table 11, n=10 column. No empirical dataset is needed.
requirements.compute: Proposed search cap: 4 CPU-hours, 8 GiB RAM and 100 starts. A candidate has twenty real coordinates and 120 triangle constraints. Exact witness checking is small compared with unrestricted global optimization; no cost or runtime has been measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Ordinary Euclidean geometry and exact or outward-rounded arithmetic. Boundary patterns and determinant-sign patterns are not assumed universally.

methods: Max-min numerical optimization without compulsory boundary occupancy
Interval branch-and-bound for explicitly bounded regions
obstacles: Rounded coordinates can destroy an apparent improvement.
Solver feasibility tolerances can exceed the claimed improvement.
Fixing eight boundary points without proof restricts the global problem.
A local maximum does not provide an unrestricted upper bound.
Literature record claims may lag newer constructions.

steps: Retrieve the reference n=10 column and verify the interpretation of its algebraic parameters.
Check all candidate coordinates belong to the square, using exact arithmetic or outward-rounded intervals.
Independently enumerate all 120 unsigned determinant areas.
Certify a strict comparison with L; do not compare rounded decimal displays.
For an upper bound, review the full domain cover, every pruning inequality and every claimed symmetry reduction.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate for an exact lower-bound witness; high for a global proof. Optimization certificates require scrutiny of tolerances and omitted regions.
validation.statement_alignment: The full target allows arbitrary real coordinates. A rational grid, a chosen boundary pattern or a finite set of starts is only a search restriction and cannot support universal nonexistence.

known_attempts: The 2002 Comellas-Yebra arrangement is reproduced with attribution in the 2026 preprint. The 2025 and 2026 papers discuss computational formulations; their reported computations are not project or model evaluations.
unresolved_checks: Independently check the published n=10 algebraic witness before using it as a numerical baseline.

Identify and check a rigorous unrestricted upper bound before using one in a proof; distinguish numerical solver bounds from exact optimality and account for the precision qualification in Sudermann-Merx v2, Section 4.1.
Check newer exact constructions and unrestricted bounds before a novelty claim.
Reconcile solver-objective and recomputed-area discrepancies rather than treating them as distinct certified records.

status_search.result: The scoped search through 2026-10-14 found no authoritative resolution of unrestricted n=10 optimality. The 2026-10-17 version check inspected Sudermann-Merx v2, whose Section 7 still identifies n=10 certification as an open direction; Section 4.1 limits the reported optimization certificates to numerical precision. This version check does not replace or extend the earlier search into an exhaustive status review.
status_search.limitations: The 2026-10-17 check concerns the cited version and relevant passages, not an independent audit of optimization certificates or a complete survey of later and unpublished records. The strongest rigorously justified unrestricted upper bound remains to be checked.
